subject: No-Training Warranty: Data TTL and Snapshot Handling for FinBank Pilot
messages:
From: Jacob Lee <jacob.lee@finbank.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: security@finbank.com
Date: Fri, 8 Mar 2029 15:12:00 -0000
Subject: Clarify training/retention for pilot - specific asks

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — FinBank's security and procurement teams want a concise write-up of a few items before we sign the pilot SOW. Short bullets below; please confirm or correct: 

- "Do you train models on customer content?" (we need a clear contract-friendly sentence)

- Can you provide a signed attestation we don't train on FinBank data for hosted API?

Procurement also attached a short set of questions (procurement_questions.docx) — can you loop in engineering/security here or point us to a runbook?

Appreciate the clarity — Jacob

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jacob Lee <jacob.lee@finbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 8 Mar 2029 17:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Clarify training/retention for pilot - specific asks

Hi Jacob —

Short answer up front: for our hosted Redwood API we do not use customer content to train or update production model weights. We can provide a signed non-training attestation for the pilot.

More detail (summarized):
- Training usage: Customer content is not fed back into model training pipelines for our hosted inference tier. We maintain a separate, curated model catalog and any model improvements are developed from public/controlled datasets and internal research — not customer prompt-response pairs.
- Request logs and telemetry: Default retention is 30 days for request-level logs and aggregated telemetry. These are retained for monitoring and billing; longer windows can be negotiated for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Customer content (uploaded files, conversation transcripts): Content is retained per the customer-configured TTL. By default for pilots we retain content for 90 days unless otherwise specified in the SOW.
- Debug snapshots & backups: Ephemeral debug snapshots exist only for troubleshooting and are scoped to the incident. Default snapshot retention is 7 days; backups for infrastructure snapshots are retained 14 days and are not used for training. See attached snapshot-retention-diagram.png for flow.
- Delete requests & tombstones: When FinBank requests deletion, we mark customer content as tombstoned within 24 hours, remove it from serving paths (e.g., caches, live indices) within 72 hours, and schedule full erasure from backups and debug artifacts within 30 days. We can accelerate timelines for Dedicated/Private by contract.

Attachments: non-training-attestation.pdf (draft), snapshot-retention-diagram.png

Next steps: I'll hand off the technical follow-ups to Mina (cc'd) to confirm encryption/backups details and provide suggested procurement language. If procurement wants the attestation as a standalone exhibit we can route to legal.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Jacob Lee <jacob.lee@finbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 9 Mar 2029 18:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Clarify training/retention for pilot - specific asks

Hi Jacob — looping in the infra/security runbook details and procurement language suggestions. Quick technical clarifications below.

- Encryption/backups: All backups and snapshots are encrypted at rest with customer-segregated keys for Dedicated customers; for hosted API we use KMS-managed keys. Backups contain customer content only where required to restore service; default backup retention is 14 days and those backups are rotated/overwritten on schedule. Backups are not used as input to training or fine-tuning.

- Snapshot types:
  * Automated ephemeral snapshots: transient artifacts created by the runtime when a node crashes. These may contain request context necessary for debugging; default retention = 7 days, then auto-pruned.
  * Support snapshots: deliberately captured by an engineer during an investigation; retention = 7 days unless extended by incident handling policy.
  * Persistent archival backups: scheduled snapshots of disk state; retention = 14 days (default).

- KV cache & model state: KV caches are in-memory by design and not persisted to durable training datasets. Model weights are immutable in the hosted inference tier — we do not apply customer data to update weights or build derivatives.

- Delete/tombstone mechanics:
  1) Tombstone: mark customer objects as deleted in metadata (within 24 hours).
  2) Remove from serving/caches: purge live caches and indexes (within 72 hours).
  3) Final erasure: scheduled job removes objects from backups/snapshots per retention window (target = 30 days). We provide a confirmation report when erasure completes.

- Procurement-friendly contract language (suggested):
  "Provider will not use Customer Content from the Services to train, fine-tune, or improve any machine learning models, directly or indirectly. Provider may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for capacity planning and service improvement; such telemetry will not contain Customer Content or PII."

I attached an internal runbook copy (runbook-data-retention-v2.md) and can export a sanitized, signable attestation for legal. If FinBank requires shorter erasure timelines we can evaluate with product/legal for the pilot.

Cheers,
Mina Haddad
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
